questions.title: Which national team will win the first semifinal of the 2026 FIFA World Cup, scheduled for July 14?
questions.background: The winners of the World Cup's two semifinals advance to the championship match.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : FIFA's official match result, corroborated by reliable news coverage if necessary. Resolution : Resolve to the national team that wins the first semifinal of the 2026 FIFA World Cup on July 14, 2026. If a penalty shootout is required, its winner counts as the match winner. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the winning national team.
questions.current_reasoning: MAJOR JULY 10 BRACKET LOCK in Dallas SF1 (Match 101, July 14): Spain defeated Belgium 2-1 in 90 minutes at SoFi Stadium (Fabian Ruiz 30', Charles De Ketelaere 41', super-sub Mikel Merino 88' after backup GK Senne Lammens spilled Pau Cubarsi's shot following Thibaut Courtois' 70' thigh injury), ELIMINATING Belgium (5.2% -> 0%) and locking in an exact two-team France vs Spain semifinal (summing to 1.000). Key July 10 fundamentals: (1) Spain extended its unbeaten streak to 37 matches, avoided extra time, picked up ZERO suspensions for SF1 (single yellows for Cubarsi 43' and Laporte 90+3' wipe cleanly after QF), and beat France in both Euro 2024 SF (2-1) and 2025 UEFA Nations League SF (5-4); (2) France brings 6/6 wins, 3 straight knockout clean sheets, 5 days rest vs Spain's 4, zero suspensions, and reassuring July 10 updates from Kylian Mbappe ('minor ankle injury, but I'm completely fine') and Deschamps ('nothing serious'); (3) SI.com's July 10 opening SF1 odds price France -144 / Spain +118 To Advance (56.3% prop / 56.7% power -> 56.5% FRA / 43.5% ESP) and +130/+220/+220 3-way (~56.2%/43.8%). Blending SI.com opening odds (56.5%/43.5%) 50/50 with our July 10 4-model ensemble (57.2%/42.8%) shifts Spain +0.124 to 0.432 and trims France -0.072 to 0.568.

local_articles.title: ‘Final before final’: France face Spain in World Cup blockbuster
local_articles.snippet: DALLAS – Spain will attempt to neutralise one of the most potent attacking arsenals in World Cup history on July 14 when they take on France in a heavyweight semi-final showdown. The reigning European champions and Didier Deschamps’ French team face off at the AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas, in what is seen by many as a ‘final before the final’ featuring the two best sides left in the tournament. In the blue corner are France, who have progressed serenely to the last four on the back of a multi-pronged strike-force spearheaded by captain Kylian Mbappe – he has scored eight goals in six games. Mbappe’s supporting cast includes Bayern Munich star Michael Olise, Ballon D’Or winner Ousmane Dembele and Paris Saint-Germain duo Bradley Barcola and Desire Doue. questions.title: Who will win the Most Valuable Player award at the 2026 MLB All-Star Game?
questions.background: The MLB All-Star Game is an annual exhibition between the American League and National League. Its Most Valuable Player award recognizes an individual player's performance in the game.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : MLB's official announcement of the 2026 All-Star Game MVP, corroborated by contemporaneous reputable news reporting. Resolution Timing : The question resolves when the MVP recipient is publicly announced following the 2026 All-Star Game, expected in July 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The full name of the player awarded the game's MVP honor.

AL starting DH Yordan Alvarez (AL-leading 29 HRs) rises to #2 (0.060 -> 0.075) as the centerpiece of a Judge-less AL lineup. NL starting OF Juan Soto (homered July 9, prime lefty power in Philly) enters at 0.065, AL starting SS Bobby Witt Jr. (homered July 9, top-of-order PAs) ticks up (0.050 -> 0.055), and AL starting 3B Junior Caminero (27 HRs, 438-ft HR July 9, Home Run Derby slugger) enters at 0.050. Sum 0.330, leaving 67% across ~50+ other All-Stars including Vladimir Guerrero Jr., Freddie Freeman, Bryce Harper, newly healthy South Jersey native Mike Trout (homered July 8 in return from IL), Brandon Marsh, Ben Rice (28 HRs), and pitchers.

questions.title: Which senior Chinese official will hold talks with Jo Yong Won in Pyongyang in the first half of July 2026?
questions.background: Jo Yong Won is a senior official in North Korea's governing Workers' Party. Chinese President Xi Jinping visited North Korea in June 2026 as Beijing and Pyongyang sought closer ties.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : KCNA, as reported by Reuters, identifying the senior Chinese official holding talks with Jo Yong Won in Pyongyang between July 1 and July 15, 2026, inclusive. Resolution Date : 2026-07-16 Accepted Answer Format : string (name). Answer with the Chinese official's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Key 2026-07-11/12 Yonhap (Korean and English) and KCNA updates: (1) DPRK Premier Pak Thae-song's delegation completed its July 10-12 Beijing trip for the 65th anniversary of the 1961 China-DPRK Treaty and returned to Pyongyang on July 12, with no reciprocal Chinese PSC delegation yet announced. (2) Crucially, Yonhap Korean (July 12, 07:16 KST) confirms that NPC Standing Committee Chair Zhao Leji (PSC #3, previously 0.075) ALSO hosted Pak Thae-song in Beijing during July 10-11 alongside Xi Jinping (#1), Li Qiang (#2), and Cai Qi (#5), while FM Wang Yi exchanged treaty messages with Choe Son Hui. Combined with Zhao Leji's April 2024 Pyongyang trip, his Beijing hosting role eliminates him from top-5 contention (dropped to ~0.015). (3) With the July 11 anniversary having passed without a simultaneous treaty-day Chinese PSC visit to Pyongyang and only July 12-15 remaining for bilateral talks specifically with WPK Presidium Secretary and Organization Guidance Dept chief Jo Yong Won, CPC Central Organization Dept head and Politburo/Secretariat member Shi Taifeng rises to #1 (0.14 -> 0.16) as Jo Yong Won's exact institutional party counterpart. Executive Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang trims slightly to #2 (0.16 -> 0.14) and CPPCC Chair Wang Huning holds at 0.13 as unconflicted PSC envoys for a staggered post-visit trip, IDCPC Minister Liu Haixing holds at 0.11 for CPC-WPK summit follow-up, and CCDI Secretary Li Xi (PSC #7, the third unconflicted PSC member and a party-discipline/governance peer to Jo Yong Won) enters at #5 (0.08). Top-5 sum = 0.62, keeping 38% residual across Liu Guozhong, Li Hongzhong, Li Shulei, Chen Wenqing, Zhang Guoqing, He Lifeng, Wang Yi, Cai Qi, Wang Yajun, and other senior officials.

questions.title: Which U.S. state will be the first to impose a statewide moratorium on construction of large new hyperscale data centres?
questions.background: Hyperscale data centres are large facilities designed to provide computing and storage capacity at massive scale. Their development can place substantial demands on electricity grids and water supplies.
questions.resolution_criteria: Qualifying Event : Resolve to the first U.S. state to formally impose, by December 31, 2026, a statewide temporary moratorium on construction or permitting of large new hyperscale data centres. Proposed legislation, vetoed measures, and restrictions limited to individual municipalities do not qualify. Source of Truth : Official state-government announcements, corroborated by reliable contemporaneous news reporting. Resolution occurs when the qualifying moratorium is publicly announced as imposed. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the state.
questions.current_reasoning: July 1-3 reporting (Cliff Daily, New Pine Plains Herald, Highlands Current) confirms New York's Responsible Data Center Development Act (S10642/A11560, passed Senate 44-16 and Assembly 102-39 on June 4) has still not been formally delivered to Gov. Kathy Hochul, which policy analysts read as active chapter-amendment negotiations signaling Hochul is likely to sign a narrowed version (higher MW threshold/in-progress carve-outs, still qualifying as a statewide moratorium on large new hyperscale data centers) rather than issue an outright veto. Progressive NY primary victories and early-July heatwave power-conservation alerts further raise election-year pressure on Hochul ahead of November, while no competing state passed a statewide construction moratorium through July 6 (VA/FL/IL July 1 measures were tax/tariff/incentive policies; MN and MI actions remain municipal only; Maine's bill was already vetoed with override failed). Raising New York from 0.74 to 0.79 (retaining ~21% veto/collapse/other-state risk) and reallocating secondary slots to active full-time legislatures (Michigan 0.04, Pennsylvania 0.03, California 0.03, New Jersey 0.02; 9% residual).
